documents.unit: Thomas Jefferson University (student policy handbook, academic policies)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Policy)
documents.summary: A short university-wide handbook policy (created 2023) that leaves the decision on generative AI to faculty, to be recorded in each course syllabus as either permitted (with citation) or restricted. Students own their work and must acknowledge AI use, embedded assistive tools remain usable unless prohibited, and violations fall under the Academic Integrity Policy.
documents.stance_why: The policy says GAI use "is under the purview of the faculty ... and is documented in the course syllabus" and offers two categories, "Permitted Use of GAI" and "Restricted Use of GAI"; it sets no default itself, so it delegates and lists these two as tiers.

units.why: The Purpose section says the policy "defines the acceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in academic courses", an institution-level statement of purpose and scope, so P56 fits better than P61 (which is about definitions).
units.resolution_why: A coded actor admin, B coded all. Both agree on P56/general/informs. The Purpose sentence states what the policy is for and is not addressed to an office, so the final actor is all.
units.anchor: defines the acceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) in academic courses

units.why: The Policy sentence says "Use of GAI beyond the approved instance ... is a violation of academic integrity", classifying unapproved GAI use as misconduct, which is P36.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this as a separate unit (B merged the whole sentence into one unit anchored on the citation clause). The sentence states two rules: use beyond the approved instance, and use lacking citation. Keeping both separate follows the one-policy-per-unit rule. This one is P36; the citation clause is P28 below. Modality is must-not since students may not use GAI beyond what is approved.
units.anchor: Use of GAI beyond the approved instance

units.why: The same sentence makes use "lacking appropriate citation" "a violation of academic integrity", so failing to cite is itself the violation; this is P28 (nondisclosure as violation), not P36, which covers unauthorized use generally, and not P24, the positive duty to disclose, coded separately.
units.resolution_why: A coded P28/must/restrict, B coded P36/must-not/prohibit. The source says AI use "lacking appropriate citation is a violation of academic integrity". That is how nondisclosure affects integrity, matching P28; unauthorized use is handled in the preceding unit as P36. Modality is must-not (a prohibition on uncited use) and the stance is restrict, because use remains allowed with citation.
units.anchor: lacking appropriate citation is a violation of academic integrity
